reference: GNU coreutils sync for named private regular files only; Bash metadata contracts. Global sync, syncfs, and injected I/O failures remain deferred.
coverage: Bash resolves sync as a builtin with an empty candidate PATH.
Bash type metadata exposes only the sync builtin in the fixture environment.
The configured short help synopsis and long sync documentation match the pinned stock loadable contract.
Deferred operation requirements cover global sync, named-file fsync, per-file failures, and option parsing behind a closed disposable-VM syscall mock.
Named-file synchronization, multiple operands, read-only files, missing-path continuation, and -- on a dash-leading file; no global flush.
exclusions: Global sync and syncfs are deferred: they can flush filesystems beyond private operands. Durability and injected I/O failures require a disposable VM/syscall mock.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash classifies the loaded sync command as a builtin; the expected type label is Bash builtin metadata.
Confirm type reports the builtin resolution when candidate PATH is empty, as configured by the harness.
Check the short help synopsis against the configured short-help text for sync in the pinned Bash-OS loadable list.
Check the complete long help text against the pinned GNU Bash loadable's documented summary, named-file behavior, no-operand behavior, and exit status.
cases.stdout:
sync: sync
    Sync disks or specified files.
    
    If one or more FILEs is supplied, force completion of pending writes
    to those files. Otherwise, force completion of any pending disk
    writes.
    
    Exit Status: zero unless any FILE could not be synced.

cases.purpose: Verify the no-operand form's global synchronization call and status behavior without flushing the host filesystem.
Fault-injected open fallback and descriptor lifetime beyond successful named-file comparisons.
Verify file-specific diagnostics, continuation across multiple operands, and aggregate failure status under injected I/O errors.
Both parsers reject an unknown option before any sync/open/fsync call. The -- dash-leading named-file operation is covered separately by dash-private-file.
Synchronize two relative regular files and compare bytes, status and tree.
cases.script:
printf one > one
printf two > two
sync one two
printf 'named sync complete\n'

cases.purpose: A file with read-only permissions may still be synchronized.
cases.script:
printf data > item
chmod 400 item
sync item

cases.purpose: A missing middle operand fails with a diagnostic while private files are preserved.
cases.script:
printf first > first
printf last > last
sync first absent last

cases.purpose: The option terminator permits a private dash-leading filename.
